rationale: The agent verified identity properly using full name and ZIP after the provided email failed, matching a single user. It used read-only tools to fetch user and order details before taking any action. It correctly stated that split payments aren’t supported, identified the most expensive item and its price from the order, and handled the user’s request sequence. When the user asked to remove an item, the agent explained system limitations and offered allowed alternatives. Before performing an order-changing action (cancellation), it clearly stated the intended change, requested explicit confirmation plus a reason, and only then executed the cancellation via the appropriate tool. The final confirmation aligns with tool output, and no actions were taken on the wrong account or without consent. Minor potential nits (terminology “charged” vs. authorized and a generic refund window) do not indicate policy violations or fabricated facts given the context and successful cancellation. Overall, the request was completed in line with policy.
